intent: "Stop this campaign" — incident response: never requires a lookup first and never waits for permission.
before_repeating: the campaign's state; pausing a paused campaign is a no-op, not an error.

input_schema.title: campaign.pause input
input_schema.description: One campaign: the work item's own, named at the provider by its pin or, the first time, by the planner. A reason is optional.

external_id.description: The provider's own identifier, given to link a campaign for the first time. Later calls work by the pin.

reason.description: Why it is paused. Optional, because a protective act never requires anything extra; it is Jason's record and never reaches the provider.

idempotency_key.description: The work item's own identifier: stable across every attempt, which is what makes a ledger under this key answerable.

items.description: One outcome per item, with the reason. A partial success reported as a single verdict is a defect.

campaign_external_id.description: The provider's identifier for the campaign this call paused.

campaign.description: The provider's identifier for the campaign this call paused, pinned so no later call has to name it again.

failure_codes.when: The provider holds no campaign under the identifier this call carried.
The provider will not pause this campaign: it is archived, or it never started. `details.provider_code` carries the provider's own word where it gave one.
The vendor tool refused the call or never started, so nothing the operation asks for was ever attempted. Repeating it runs the same broken call.
The plugin's own credential does not let it pause campaigns for this account.
The provider refused the pause for now and it may be attempted again.
The provider could not be reached, or answered with a failure on its own side, before anything was written.
The provider was called and no answer arrived, so the campaign may already be paused. Pausing a paused campaign changes nothing, so the next attempt simply asks again.

The provider refused this call for a reason outside the work item — the account's money or plan, an allowance it counts, a credential it no longer accepts, a channel disconnected or paused — and did nothing for it. The failure's block says what is blocked, why and where a person clears it; a repeat once it clears is a first act. It is said even where the operation also declares an older code for the condition, which then stands for an answer the plugin cannot read as a block.

conformance: A campaign already paused changes nothing, and answers `already_paused` where the provider says it was paused before, or `paused` where the provider answers a repeated pause as a pause; the provider documents the call as idempotent, which is what makes a repeat after a lost answer safe.
A campaign that cannot be paused — archived, or never started — fails `campaign_not_pausable`, with the provider's own code under `details.provider_code` where it gave one.
Nothing beyond the campaign is required: `reason` is optional, and it is Jason's record that never reaches the provider.
A campaign named for the first time is pinned, as `campaign.get` pins it, and every later call works by the pin.
